message.abstract:
<jats:p>
            Given a planar graph
            <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>
            and a partition of the neighbors of each vertex
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            in four sets
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↗</jats:sup>
            ,
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↖</jats:sup>
            ,
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↙</jats:sup>
            , and
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↘</jats:sup>
            , the problem W
            <jats:sc>indrose</jats:sc>
            P
            <jats:sc>lanarity</jats:sc>
            asks to decide whether
            <jats:italic>G</jats:italic>
            admits a
            <jats:italic>windrose-planar drawing</jats:italic>
            , that is, a planar drawing in which (i) each neighbor
            <jats:italic>u</jats:italic>
            ∈
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↗</jats:sup>
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            is above and to the right of
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            , (ii) each neighbor
            <jats:italic>u</jats:italic>
            ∈
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↖</jats:sup>
            is above and to the left of
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            , (iii) each neighbor
            <jats:italic>u</jats:italic>
            ∈
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↙</jats:sup>
            is below and to the left of
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            , (iv) each neighbor
            <jats:italic>u</jats:italic>
            ∈
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            <jats:sup>↘</jats:sup>
            is below and to the right of
            <jats:italic>v</jats:italic>
            , and (v) edges are represented by curves that are monotone with respect to each axis. By exploiting both the horizontal and the vertical relationship among vertices, windrose-planar drawings allow us to simultaneously visualize two partial orders defined by means of the edges of the graph.
          </jats:p>
          <jats:p>
            Although the problem is
            <jats:italic>NP</jats:italic>
            -hard in the general case, we give a polynomial-time algorithm for testing whether there exists a windrose-planar drawing that respects a given combinatorial embedding. This algorithm is based on a characterization of the plane triangulations admitting a windrose-planar drawing. Furthermore, for any embedded graph with
            <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
            vertices that has a windrose-planar drawing, we can construct one with at most one bend per edge and with at most 2
            <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
            −5 bends in total, which lies on the 3
            <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
            × 3
            <jats:italic>n</jats:italic>
            grid. The latter result contrasts with the fact that straight-line windrose-planar drawings may require exponential area.
          </jats:p>
title: Windrose Planarity
